head: 2cf5a4929

boundaries: the ban, mute and invite requests

notes: Group admin controls: Add Members fix, ban reason for the banned user alone, readable audit log, live admin events, no mute reason, the ban rule on the way back, Unmute with a timer.

instruments.evidence: de7bcbe8b..2cf5a4929: 4795ff233 (Add Members keeps past invitees findable and invites on Enter; banned-invite message; ban notice for the banned user; ban window hint; readable audit log with a raw toggle; mute without a reason; Unmute with a minute timer; admin events forwarded as ws-group-event), 26374adfc (ban reason to the banned user alone after commit; mute keeps no reason; ban rule on invite, add and accept with an audited lift), 2cf5a4929 (review: the ban window hint's test). Only my four en.json hunks were committed; Codex's stay unstaged. Boundaries: the ban, mute and invite requests, the group_you_were_banned and group_member_banned payloads, the restriction and audit rows, ws-group-event, the member menu, the audit log, the toast.
Read 04a7c4b7d (membership events; H7), e619a6d8c (socket event handling), b3df29afc (broadcastToGroup).

Rendered: the ban window with its hint (pane, then Cancel -- nobody banned); the Audit Log tab with its raw toggle (pane; the user confirmed the toggle works); the member menu in tests (Unmute with '2h 5m left', then '2h 4m left'); the user confirmed Add Members and the ban notice with its reason in real browsers.

Socket payloads read in Go tests for two inputs: the banned user's group_you_were_banned {conversation_id, group_name 'Live Group ban', reason 'spam'}; the remaining member's group_member_banned with no reason key. The client test covers a ban with a reason and one without (no description line).

Rows: after a mute sent with a reason, group_member_restrictions.reason is NULL and the audit details hold only duration_minutes; after an owner's invite or add of a banned user, the ban row is gone and an unban_member row holds via invite or via add; after a member's attempt, the ban row remains.

Error code group_user_banned is the same string on the server and in GroupInviteMembers; event names group_you_were_banned, group_member_banned and the four admin events match; the restrictions query key ['group-restrictions', id] is the one useGroupAdmin and the sidebar invalidate.
The client reads payload.group_name and payload.reason from group_you_were_banned, and expires_at from the restrictions list, the fields the server sets.

instruments.why: One ban rule (admitBanned) behind invite and add; the accept check is a separate refusal by design.
JSON payloads and bodies; MuteGroupMemberRequest lost its field, so an extra 'reason' is simply ignored (B4).

instruments.evidence: The error code is read from response.data.code; the test rejects with that exact shape, and a generic error still shows the old message.
The banned-invite test rejects with the shape an AxiosError carries ({response: {data: {code}}}), per the project note that the code lives in the response body.
An owner's and an admin-level invite of a banned user are accepted and lift the ban.
A member's invite or add of a banned user is refused; a banned user's accept of an older invite is refused.
Mute time-left boundaries: 12m, exactly 60 (1h 0m), 125 (2h 5m), 3 days 4 hours; a permanent mute shows Permanent; an expired mute shows Mute again.
Siblings: the existing UnbanGroupMember logs unban_member with no details; the automatic lift logs the same action with via, so the audit filter still groups them.
admitBanned's member branch and admin branch are each reached (member refused, owner lifts); the accept check is reached.
A failed ban-list read answers 500 and rolls back; a failed group-name read leaves the notice with an empty name rather than failing the ban.

instruments.why: No flag-gated path beyond anyone_can_invite, which the member test sets on.
Nothing duplicated: one helper for the ban rule, one for time left.

instruments.evidence: Every way back into a group: invite, direct add, accept -- all apply the rule (no self-join route exists). Every place a ban reason went: both ban events and the audit log -- now the banned user's event and the log only. Every place a mute reason went: the request, the restriction row, the audit log and the mute event -- all removed.

The ban lift runs inside the invite's or add's transaction, so a failed invite leaves the ban in place; both ban events wait for the commit, so nobody hears of a ban that failed (the old code told the banned user first).
Declining an owner's invite leaves the user unbanned but outside the group; a new invite is needed to join. Said to the user.
adm-r1-ban-hint-untested: with the hint removed, the ban window test fails 'Unable to find ... Only the banned user sees this reason'; tsc -b clean with the patch.
go build, go vet (handlers, integration) and gofmt clean; tsc -b, eslint and the i18n check clean.
The finding came from C10, already a row.

The user ran Add Members, the ban reason notice and the raw toggle in real browsers and reported them working. The ban rule on re-invite and the Unmute timer are not yet run in a browser; said to the user.
The ban handler used to notify the banned user before the transaction; both events now go out after the commit.
The Unmute item puts the time left beside the label with justify-between in the 12rem menu; the longest value, '30d 23h left', fits beside 'Unmute'.
The toast store is module state; addToast is now exported for the socket handler, and every change still notifies the listeners.
Go runs with -v and TEST_DATABASE_URL: the ban rule, ban reason, invite, join and membership tests PASS; the handler group, ban and mute tests PASS; 0 SKIP.

The user's requests: the banned user sees the reason and the ban window says so (yes); the reason goes to nobody else (yes); readable audit log with a raw toggle in the same panel (yes); live admin updates (yes); no mute reason (yes); a member cannot bring a banned user back, an admin's add lifts the ban and logs it (yes); Unmute with a timer to the minute (yes).

instruments.why: One entry point per side effect.
The ban notice is a toast in the existing container; no new layer.

instruments.evidence: Ran every test file that imports or mocks GroupDetailsSidebar, GroupInviteMembers, GroupAuditLog, adminGroupsService, MessagesPage or MuteUserModal: 9 files, 59 passed, 1 old skip; the WebSocketContext tests (14); and the Go handler tests for groups, bans and mutes.
Earlier controls: grpact-r1-* target groups.go's announceLeave and MessagesPage/WebSocketContext lines, still present and applying; re-checked with git apply --check.
useMinuteClock clears its interval on unmount and when the mute has no end time.
The Go tests run the real handlers and hub.
Shuffled the changed frontend test files in earlier runs; the new files hold no shared mutable state beyond per-test mocks.
Producers of group_you_were_banned: BanGroupMember only. Of the restrictions the menu reads: mute and unmute, which invalidate the same key, and the forwarded admin events.

Found the finding: removed each added line on both sides. Backend -- the ban rule on invite and on add, the accept check, both unban audit entries, the reason on each ban event, the mute reason in the log -- each fails its test. Frontend -- forwarding of muted and slow mode, the ban toast, the banned-invite message, the audit via text, the Unmute click -- each fails a test; the ban window hint did not.
The new tests' absence checks run after a positive settled sign (the readable entry found, the restrictions fetched, the menu opened).

findings.summary: The ban window's line saying only the banned user sees the reason, which the user asked for, had no test: removing it left every test green.

control.observed: FAIL: Unable to find 'Only the banned user sees this reason. It is also kept in the audit log.'
